The most memorable parts of YC Startup School weren't any of the talks. This past weekend, I joined thousands of founders at Chase Center for two days of speakers, events, and meeting people. I went in almost not knowing a single person there, which meant two straight days of walking up to strangers and starting from nothing. That ended up being the best part, as the moments I remember most were the ones that weren’t on the schedule. The arena somehow roaring louder for Boris Cherny announcing free Claude Max than it did when Sam and Jensen walked in: six thousand founders, two of the most recognizable people in tech on schedule that weekend, and the roof came off for a subscription. The stampede after Sam's talk, six thousand of us running for the same buses and trains, and then the two hours we spent standing in the AWS afterparty line, which sounds miserable on paper but somehow turned into the best conversation I had all weekend. Somewhere in the middle of all of that was my first hackathon ever, the YC overnight batch hosted by Corgi and Vercel, where my team, strangers who I paired up with last minute, placed 3rd out of 1500 in the main track. Paul Lacarriere , Saahith, and Karthik, thank you for staying up the entire night and actually finishing our project instead of just talking about it. https://lnkd.in/gNxKRipS I showed up planning to network, and I think I'd assumed the point of a room like that was to collect people who might be useful to you later, and it isn't, or at least it wasn't for me, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗜 𝗸𝗲𝗽𝘁 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘂𝗽 𝗻𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗜 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗲𝗹𝘁 𝗮 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵. Somehow, the best connections happened whenever I stopped trying to force them. Can't wait to see everyone again next year!

If AI can translate any language in real time, why even learn one? And honestly… why build a language learning company? I thought about this a lot after trying Google's latest AI translation models ( launched March 2026) in Thailand. They were incredible for transactional moments: ordering food, asking for directions, getting from A to B. But translation isn't understanding. Especially for children, learning another language comes with rich cognitive benefits and can shape how they think, pay attention, and understand the world around them. You miss the little things, the tone, the timing, the inside jokes. You’re always a step behind the moment. AI will remove the need to translate languages. I don't think it removes the reason to learn them. #parrot #languagelearning #ai

Over 1 billion students around the world are likely taught a language in school every year. But why do we even teach languages? And should we? Students spend years studying them alongside subjects like math and science… yet most still can't speak. Maybe it's time to rethink language education entirely. #parrot #languagelearning #cambridgeuniversity

“Why would we compete with a $6B giant?” That was the question I asked Erik Dahl and Julia Hudea asking when we started Parrot (YC F25) . So before building, we interviewed 186 Duolingo users to understand what they loved, what kept them coming back, and where they still felt stuck. The pattern was surprisingly clear: people loved the streaks, the ease, and the fun - but many still didn’t feel like they could understand real people speaking. That became the bet behind Parrot: make learning languages feel as natural and addictive as scrolling TikTok, but built around real native videos and comprehensible input. ---- 1. We've helped hundreds of people replace some of their scrolling habits with the dream to learn a second language, and actually speak it 2. We've tripled our 2025 revenue and on track to 7x by the end of the year 3. We're hiring for our founding engineer position (link in the comments) 4. Grown to over 400K users 5. The Parrot Nest and the team located in the heart of San Francisco Erik Dahl Julia Hudea

Today, I'm excited to announce our newest product at Blueberry 🫐 Over the past few months, Blueberry has been powering some of the biggest brands in the world. Now, we’re excited to unveil something incredible: the world’s first commerce agent that sells for you. Here's how it works. You give Blueberry a goal, and it gets to work. It can be as straightforward as “Sell out my Fourth of July sale”. Blueberry’s AI agents find everyone engaging with your brand, research who they actually are, and send the right DM at the right moment to turn that attention into sales. Not a generic "here's 10% off" blast. But a message that feels like it was written by someone who actually understands them and their needs. It’s that simple. This isn’t theoretical, by the way. Our customers are already using Blueberry to drive millions in sales and optimize every marketing flow imaginable — from turning social followers to CRM contacts to capturing intent-signals to convert customers, pushing first-party data across their CDPs, and more. This product was only made possible by the incredible team I get to work with daily. They've been hard at work bringing Blueberry to life, and helping tell our story for the past few months. Clerked already automates payables. Now, finance leaders can use natural language to instantly build custom reports about their spend. "Break down forklift spend by plant and flag where I'm overpaying." "Which items am I buying from more than one vendor?" "Find the vendors with open POs that haven't invoiced us this month, and chase them." One customer found he was buying the same product from three vendors at three different prices. He went back to all three, told them he was consolidating to one, and asked for their best number. Another had five analysts spending half their time building plant-level spend reports by hand. That work is gone. For the first time ever, make your AP platform save you more and more. Learn more at clerked.ai

Average DITL of an viral app founder: 6am - alarm, already 14 unread messages 6:11am - chug coffee and open laptop 6:23am - dashboard won't load (mild panic), refresh, we're fine 8am - a creator with a video going live today ghosts 9am - back-to-back-to-back calls. Sign a creator on the first one, pass on the next two 10am - a post we paid four figures for is doing nothing 11am - a post we paid pennies for is going viral, quick dopamine hit 12pm - "lunch" aka a protein bar and another coffee while renegotiating a deal 1pm - the ghost from 8am resurfaces. Video's up and it's a banger, crisis over 2pm - three new fires, put out two. Prays 3pm - takes a 15-min walk to see the sun 4pm - downloads spike, no idea why. Spend 20 minutes trying to find out, gives up for now 5pm - researching new creators to reach out to 7pm - dinner with girlfriend, leaves phone in office for 20 mins (borderline illegal) 9pm - 3rd fire from earlier gets resolved 10pm - figures out what caused the spike, 2nd dopamine hit 11pm - last look at the numbers, tell myself I'll sleep early tomorrow (I won't) This work is not for the faint of heart.
